headline: Google's Liz Reid says readers lose interest in shallow pages
dek: On the FOMO Sapiens podcast, published November 19, Google's head of Search Elizabeth Reid said people "don't want purely AI, they want AI in the web." She described less interest in pages that only recite a surface fact, using a page that just gives Japan's time zone as her example. Content built on personal expertise, experience or in-depth research still draws an audience, she said.
why: This lines up with Google's recent warning against generic Top 10 posts. Reid spoke about what people want to read, though, and gave no traffic or ranking figures, so it stands as Google's stated view with no measured results behind it.
doThis: Go through your site and flag pages that only restate a simple fact (hours, definitions, a list anyone could write). Pick one and add something only you know, such as a real customer question, a local detail or a photo from your own work.
